open_questions: Depth scatter amplitude 139.5% between sectors remains unexplained – should be tested with ground-based transit photometry to confirm consistent depth
Centroid remains inconclusive (no sector with clear difference image) – higher-resolution time-series or simultaneous multi-colour photometry would confirm on-target
Radius uncertainty 0.402 vs 0.463-0.467 Rsun from Gaia changes Rp 3.04 to 3.5 Re – spectroscopic radius with density match would refine size
dossier.public_summary: A 3% dip lasting 3.5 hours repeats every 13.3 days as a small 3-Earth-radius, flat-bottomed transit around a 97-parsec M dwarf. There is no sign of a second eclipse or odd-even difference, the depth scatter between sectors matches the star's spotty variability, and Gaia shows the star is larger than TIC, fixing the long duration. The dip is best explained by a Neptune-size planet despite deep variability.

reasons.why: Sub-Saturn size and non-grazing impact parameter fit_b 0.08588 favours a planet over a V-shaped or grazing stellar eclipse; on-target flat bottom favours planet.
Strongly flat-bottomed transit, opposite of V-shaped EB/grazing signature.
No significant odd/even difference and no significant secondary; excludes binary at twice period and close stellar companion.
Duration longer than central with TIC M-dwarf radius is explained by Gaia radius 15% larger; stellar density penalty 39.54 reduces and fit is consistent with planet transit, not density mismatch.

reasons.why: Large depth scatter is expected for this low-TEFF 3314 K M dwarf: variability_chi2_dof 0.8119 within transit but sector 8 depth 1581 ppm err 770, sectors 34 6595 err 875, 61 8769 err 1080, 88 3666 err 1357. This is spot/instrument systematics, not EB depth change, and does not outweigh flat shape, no odd/even, no secondary, small planet size and consistent duration with Gaia radius. Low ML rank reflects variability but similar signals have been planets.
